CostBasis.description:
The operator's own cost per vehicle-hour, plus where that rate came from.

`avoidable_share_low`/`high` are the fraction of that rate which actually
falls when a vehicle-hour is removed -- the fixed-versus-variable split.
They have NO default: nobody outside the operator's finance office knows
it, and inventing one is how a teardown becomes a lie in front of a
director who knows their books. Absent them, the teardown reports the
accounting value of the empty time and explicitly no envelope.

source.description: Where the rate came from, verbatim, so it can be checked (e.g. an NTD filing line).
source.title: Source

CostBasis.title: CostBasis

CostEnvelope.description:
HOW MUCH -- and how much of that is not a promise.

`value_at_full_cost` is arithmetic on the operator's own rate: empty hours
times cost per vehicle-hour. It is the accounting value of the time, never
a saving. `modelled_envelope_low`/`high` apply the modelled reduction and
the operator's own fixed-versus-variable split, and are None (with
`envelope_basis` saying so) when that split was not supplied.

hedge.default: Modelled envelope, not guaranteed cash: how much of this is genuinely recoverable depends on the operator's fixed-versus-variable split -- fixed costs (salaries, depreciation, admin) do not fall proportionally with vehicle-hours removed. The value at full cost below is the accounting value of the empty time at the operator's own rate, not a saving.
hedge.title: Hedge

CostEnvelope.title: CostEnvelope

DeadheadTeardown.description:
The structured answer to "which hours, which runs, how much".

`causal_proof` is fixed False and raises if set: a teardown measures where
empty time sat in records that were already produced; it says nothing about
what caused it or what removing it would achieve.

attributed_run_count.description: How many identified runs contributed any empty time at all -- the full ranking's length before top_n truncation, so a reader can see what the top-N is a top-N of.
attributed_run_count.title: Attributed Run Count

by_day_of_week_and_hour.title: By Day Of Week And Hour

interpretation.default: Modelled teardown, not causal proof and not a promised saving. This localises non-revenue (empty) vehicle time to hours, days and runs from the trip-level records supplied; it shows where empty time sat, not that any of it was avoidable. Any money figure is the accounting value of that time at the operator's own cost per vehicle-hour, hedged by the fixed-versus-variable split. Every figure is re-derivable from this manifest's inputs and method.
interpretation.title: Interpretation

DeadheadTeardown.title: DeadheadTeardown

DecisionAlternative.description:
A candidate assignment considered (and, usually, rejected) during a
schedule run -- required so "why not the alternatives" is answerable.
DecisionAlternative.title: DecisionAlternative

DecisionEvent.description:
One entry in the append-only, hash-chained decision ledger.

See architecture/decisions/0003-append-only-hash-chained-event-log.md:
tamper-evident, not immutable, not a compliance certificate.
DecisionEvent.title: DecisionEvent

EvidencePack.description: A portable, JSON-serializable evidence bundle for one aggregate.
EvidencePack.title: EvidencePack

EvidencePacket.description:
Evidence IR v0.1: the reconstructed narrative for one aggregate's full
decision history. Built only from an event history, raw storage rows, and
(if it exists yet) an Outcome -- this packet reorganizes already-recorded
facts, it never derives a new one about the world.
EvidencePacket.title: EvidencePacket

InputRecord.description:
One input the teardown consumed, and where it came from, so the figure
it feeds can be checked against the operator's own source.
InputRecord.title: InputRecord

KnownInput.description:
What was known when one RECOMMENDATION event was generated -- that
event's own payload and reason codes, verbatim. Never supplemented with
information not actually recorded at that sequence.
KnownInput.title: KnownInput

MethodStep.description:
One step of the arithmetic actually applied, stated precisely enough to
be re-run by hand on the same export.
MethodStep.title: MethodStep

OperatorExportValidationRequest.description:
Body for `POST /operator-exports/validate`: a SAMPLE of an operator's
export, plus the `column_map` they intend to send it with.

`rows` are raw export rows exactly as the agency's extract produces them --
the same `list[dict]` the adapter takes. They are checked and discarded;
see the endpoint docstring for what "discarded" means precisely.
OperatorExportValidationRequest.title: OperatorExportValidationRequest

OperatorExportValidationResponse.description:
The dry-run verdict on a sample export.

`persisted` is fixed False and RAISES if set True, the same structural
refusal `DeadheadTeardown.causal_proof` uses: the non-persistence promise is
encoded in the response model, not only in prose.

persistence_note.default: Nothing from this request was stored. The rows were parsed in memory against an ephemeral tenant id that belongs to no store, the resulting canonical records were discarded without ever being written, and no value from any row is echoed back below -- only column NAMES, counts and reasons.
persistence_note.title: Persistence Note

OperatorExportValidationResponse.title: OperatorExportValidationResponse

Outcome.description:
What actually happened to one service request.

``vehicle_ref``/``run_ref`` are the CANONICAL HOME ADR-0038 found missing.
Before them, the vehicle/run assignment lived only on the Connect-layer
``OperatorTripRecord`` and was recorded as a ``dropped`` semantic loss on
every row -- so the single field the whole deadhead teardown depends on
(``packages/replay/teardown.py`` chains ONE vehicle's consecutive trips;
ADR-0038 makes ``vehicle_ref``-or-``run_ref`` a mandatory intake column for
exactly that reason) survived the in-memory handoff and would NOT have
survived a write to MilexiumDB.

WHY HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE. Which vehicle/run performed (or was assigned and
did not perform) a trip is a fact about *what happened*, not about what was
asked for, so it belongs on the outcome record -- sitting directly beside
``deadhead_minutes``, the field derived from chaining it. It is deliberately
NOT duplicated onto ``ServiceRequest``: one fact, one home, so the two can
never disagree. A teardown needing the request's own times joins on
``(tenant_id, request_id)``.

WHY PLAIN STRINGS, NOT ``VehicleId``. These name the SOURCE SYSTEM's entities
(an operator's own vehicle number, run or block id), not a Milexium
``Vehicle`` aggregate -- the same reason ``VehicleObservation.vehicle_ref`` is
a plain string. Typing them as ``VehicleId`` would assert a canonical
aggregate that no operator export creates.

Both are optional and BOTH may be absent: a trip whose export named neither
is unattributable, and the teardown reports it as such rather than guessing
it onto a neighbouring run. Absent means absent; it is never back-filled.

run_ref.description: Source-system run/block identifier, as the operator writes it.
run_ref.title: Run Ref

vehicle_ref.description: Source-system vehicle identifier, as the operator writes it. Never a VehicleId.
vehicle_ref.title: Vehicle Ref

Outcome.title: Outcome

ReasonCode.description: Scheduling explanation reason codes. Never SHAP output or generated prose.
ReasonCode.title: ReasonCode

RecordDecisionRequest.description:
Body for `POST /decisions`. `actor_type` is not a field: the endpoint
fixes it to "system" (a recommendation is a system act), exactly as
`MilexiumClient.record_decision` does.
RecordDecisionRequest.title: RecordDecisionRequest

RecordOverrideRequest.description:
Body for `POST /decisions/{aggregate_id}/overrides`. `aggregate_id` comes
from the path; `actor_id` (the human overriding) is required, not
defaulted -- mirroring `MilexiumClient.record_override`.
RecordOverrideRequest.title: RecordOverrideRequest

RecordedEvent.description:
The wire projection of a recorded `DecisionEvent`. An API-owned model, so
the HTTP contract is decoupled from the internal canonical entity; typed
UUIDv7 ids and enums are projected to plain strings.
RecordedEvent.title: RecordedEvent

RowValidation.description:
What WOULD happen to one sample row on a real import.

`reason` is the adapter's own quarantine text, which names offending columns
by NAME and never quotes a rejected identifier's value. `pii_columns` is
derived from the adapter's redaction of its own quarantine record (the
columns it replaced with `REDACTION_MARKER`), so it reports which columns to
strip without this layer re-running -- or weakening -- the PII check.
RowValidation.title: RowValidation

RunContribution.description:
WHICH RUNS -- one run's contribution to the empty time.

`attributable` is False exactly when the export gave no run identifier;
that row is the honest "we cannot tell you which run this was" total, and
is reported outside the ranking so a top-N truncation can never bury it.
RunContribution.title: RunContribution

SemanticLossNote.description:
One semantic-loss note the adapter attached to an accepted row, projected
for the wire WITHOUT `SemanticLossRecord.source_value`.

The adapter already nulls `source_value` everywhere personal data could hide
(unmapped extensions, the rider reference). Dropping the field entirely at
the API boundary means that guarantee does not depend on the adapter's field
policy staying exactly as it is: a validation response cannot carry a source
value because the model has nowhere to put one. The `reason` text is what
the operator needs anyway -- it says what was lost and why.
SemanticLossNote.title: SemanticLossNote

TeardownBucketRow.description:
WHICH HOURS -- one clock position's empty and earning minutes, as
claimed. `day_of_week` is None on an hour-of-day-only bucket and
`hour_of_day` is None on a day-of-week-only bucket.
TeardownBucketRow.title: TeardownBucketRow

TeardownEvidence.description:
A deadhead teardown in pack-carriable form: the manifest verbatim, the
claimed figures and surfaces, and the segments those figures must follow
from.

`manifest` is the ADR-0039 `TeardownManifest` dumped verbatim as a dict --
the same convention `EvidencePack.evidence` already uses for the
`EvidencePacket`, and the reason a pack can be loaded and re-derived with no
`packages.replay` import anywhere in the verification path.

`data_provenance` restates the manifest's provenance as a VALIDATED field
(the manifest is a verbatim record and could say anything); re-derivation
checks the two agree. It admits only "real_public" or "synthetic" -- a pack
built from real public data says so, and there is no "operator" value to
say anything else with.

note.default: This pack carries a modelled deadhead teardown together with the trip-structure segments it was computed from, so a third party can RECOMPUTE its headline figures from those segments and the manifest's declared inputs instead of trusting the recorded numbers. Re-derivation checks arithmetic, not truth: it proves the figures follow from the data supplied, never that any empty time was avoidable, that the data describes the operation faithfully, or that any money would be recovered.
note.title: Note

TeardownEvidence.title: TeardownEvidence

TeardownFigures.description:
The headline figures exactly as the teardown emitted them -- the CLAIM
that gets re-derived and checked.

Deliberately carries no input value. Every input (the cost per vehicle-hour,
the modelled reduction fraction, the operator's avoidable share) lives in
the manifest's `(name, value, source)` records, so re-derivation always runs
inputs -> figures and can never be satisfied by reading a figure back out of
the thing it is checking.

`value_at_full_cost` is the accounting value of the empty time at the
operator's own rate, NOT a saving; `hedge` carries ADR-0039's
`FIXED_COST_HEDGE` verbatim and `envelope_basis` carries its refusal to
guess a recoverable fraction when the operator's fixed-versus-variable split
was not supplied.
TeardownFigures.title: TeardownFigures

TeardownManifest.description:
Pins what a teardown used and how, so it is reproducible and auditable.

`teardown_id` is deterministic in the segments and the modelling choices:
the same export torn down the same way pins the same id.

note.default: Modelled teardown, not causal proof and not a promised saving. This localises non-revenue (empty) vehicle time to hours, days and runs from the trip-level records supplied; it shows where empty time sat, not that any of it was avoidable. Any money figure is the accounting value of that time at the operator's own cost per vehicle-hour, hedged by the fixed-versus-variable split. Every figure is re-derivable from this manifest's inputs and method.
note.title: Note

replay_discipline_note.default: Modelled comparison, not causal proof of savings. This compares the recorded or simulated outcomes of two schedules over the same request set; at least one schedule is a counterfactual that was not actually operated over that identical set, so every delta is a modelled difference between schedules, not measured proof that Milexium caused an improvement. Public aggregate data validates aggregate demand tasks, not individual dispatch. No monetary savings figure is derived.
replay_discipline_note.title: Replay Discipline Note

TeardownManifest.title: TeardownManifest

TeardownRequest.description:
Body for `POST /teardowns` -- the arguments of
`MilexiumClient.teardown_deadhead`, one-to-one.

The field list is the whole refusal surface, so read what is ABSENT:

- There is no `is_guaranteed_saving` and no `causal_proof`. `extra="forbid"`
  means sending either is a 422, not a silently ignored field -- an API that
  accepted them would be advertising a claim the analysis refuses to make.
- `data_provenance` is the `DataProvenance` Literal, which has no "operator"
  value, so an HTTP caller cannot label anything as operator data either.
- `cost_basis.avoidable_share_low/high` still have no default. Omit them and
  you get the accounting value of the empty time and NO envelope, with
  `envelope_basis` stating that the recoverable fraction is unknown.

`segments` are `VehicleSegment` models straight from `packages.replay`, not
an API-local copy, so the domain's own construction rules (UTC-aware
timestamps, end-not-before-start, the 48h parsing-artefact ceiling, and
`extra="forbid"` blocking a rider field from being attached to a segment)
are enforced on the wire rather than restated and allowed to drift.
TeardownRequest.title: TeardownRequest

TeardownRunRow.description:
WHICH RUNS -- one run's contribution, as claimed. `attributable` is False
exactly when the export carried no run reference; that row is reported
outside the ranking so a top-N truncation can never bury it. A redacted pack
masks `run_ref` to `[REDACTED]` and leaves `attributable` True: the run WAS
identified in the source, it simply is not disclosed here.
TeardownRunRow.title: TeardownRunRow

TeardownSegmentRow.description:
One embedded segment: trip STRUCTURE only -- when it started, when it
ended, whether it was earning, and which run it belonged to.

These are the same four fields ADR-0039's `VehicleSegment` carries and the
only four it reads, restated here as plain JSON-safe values so a pack can be
loaded and re-derived without importing the generator. Nothing else can ride
along: `extra="forbid"` plus a fixed four-field shape means a rider
identifier cannot be attached to a segment on its way into a pack, just as
it cannot be attached on its way into a teardown.

Timestamps are held as the ISO-8601 strings the fingerprint is computed
over, so the fingerprint is reproduced from bytes rather than from a
re-formatting of a parsed value.
TeardownSegmentRow.title: TeardownSegmentRow

TimeBucket.description:
WHICH HOURS -- empty and earning minutes at one clock position.

`day_of_week` is None on an hour-of-day-only bucket and `hour_of_day` is
None on a day-of-week-only bucket; both are set on a joint bucket. Minutes
are apportioned across hour boundaries, so the buckets in any one grouping
sum exactly to the headline totals.
TimeBucket.title: TimeBucket

VehicleSegment.description:
One contiguous block of one vehicle's time, already classified.

Trip structure only: when it started, when it ended, whether it was earning,
and which run/block/vehicle it belonged to. ``extra="forbid"`` means a rider
identifier cannot be attached to a segment at all -- construction raises.
``run_ref`` is the *source system's* identifier (a run, block or vehicle id
as the operator writes it), left as a plain string for the same reason
VehicleObservation.vehicle_ref is: it names their entity, not ours. ``None``
means the export did not say, and is honoured as "unattributable" rather
than filled in.

run_ref.description: Source-system run/block/vehicle id, or None when the export omitted it.
run_ref.title: Run Ref

VehicleSegment.title: VehicleSegment

VerifyResponse.description:
Result of the independent hash-chain check. `verified` is True iff the
verifier found zero violations -- the same meaning as the SDK's empty tuple,
not a stronger claim.
VerifyResponse.title: VerifyResponse

info.description:
Milexium HTTP API (Program M, v0.1 HTTP surface).

A thin FastAPI application that exposes the same decision loop as the
`MilexiumClient` Python SDK over HTTP, so software that is *not* written in
Python can integrate the runtime -- the "others integrate this" unlock that the
SDK began and this layer extends past the Python boundary.

It is pure composition over `packages.sdk.MilexiumClient`; it adds no domain
logic, only an HTTP contract and Pydantic request/response bodies. Every
endpoint below is a call to one SDK method -- mostly one-to-one, except
`/operator-exports/validate`, which loops `client.ingest` a row at a time so it
can attribute each verdict to a row index. The endpoint set is deliberately
narrow:

    GET  /health                                   liveness
    GET  /version                                  API / SDK / contract versions
    POST /decisions                                record a RECOMMENDATION (system act)
    POST /decisions/{aggregate_id}/overrides       record an OVERRIDE (human act)
    GET  /decisions/{aggregate_id}/evidence        the reconstructed EvidencePacket
    GET  /decisions/{aggregate_id}/evidence-pack   the portable, self-verifying EvidencePack
    GET  /decisions/{aggregate_id}/verify          independent hash-chain check
    POST /teardowns                                deadhead teardown over trip segments (ADR-0039)
    POST /operator-exports/validate                dry-run intake check on an export sample (ADR-0038)

The OpenAPI schema FastAPI serves at **/openapi.json** (human-browsable at
**/docs**) is the machine-readable API contract -- a non-Python client generates
its own bindings from it.

WHY THESE TWO GOT AN HTTP ENDPOINT AND INGESTION STILL DOES NOT
ADR-0021 excluded ingestion and forecast from HTTP for one reason: their inputs
are *Python objects and on-disk files* (a `SourceAdapter` instance; a model
registry plus xgboost artifacts), and pretending otherwise would mean inventing
a JSON stand-in for something that is not JSON. That reasoning is respected
here, not worked around -- it simply does not apply to these two:

- A `VehicleSegment` is four scalars (start, end, revenue-or-deadhead, run
  reference). It is already a JSON object; a JSON POST body is its honest
  shape, not a wrapper around one. So `POST /teardowns` takes segments inline.
- The operator-export *validation* path is configured entirely by a JSON
  `column_map` over a named, concrete adapter -- no Python object crosses the
  boundary -- and it does not ingest anything, so ADR-0021's objection (an
  adapter is a Python object) has nothing to bite on.

Deliberately NOT done, with reasons rather than silence:

- **No multipart/CSV upload on either endpoint.** Tempting for a big export,
  but it would put CSV parsing, type coercion and header handling in the API,
  which is Connect adapter work with an existing owner; it would also give the
  validation endpoint a file on disk (Starlette spools uploads), which is
  exactly what an endpoint promising to persist nothing should not have. Both
  endpoints therefore take bounded JSON and refuse oversize bodies with 413,
  pointing bulk callers at the SDK (`client.teardown_deadhead`), which has no
  size ceiling at all.
- **No "tear down my raw export" endpoint.** Turning export rows into segments
  requires deciding which rows are revenue and which are deadhead, and
  `packages.replay.teardown` deliberately refuses to infer that from geometry
  or timing -- the caller's adapter decides. An HTTP endpoint that guessed it
  would be inventing the one judgment the module refuses to make.
- **Generic ingestion and forecast endpoints.** Unchanged from ADR-0021: they
  stay on the SDK (`client.ingest`, `client.forecast`) and are Specified for
  HTTP.
- **Auth, the multi-tenant API gateway, and rate limiting.** OUT of scope
  (Specified). This app is backed by ONE `MilexiumClient` bound to ONE
  in-memory tenant; there is no per-request tenant resolution, no credential
  check, and no quota. A real deployment injects a Postgres-backed store
  (`packages.canonical` PostgresCanonicalStore) and puts tenant auth in front --
  none of which this slice fakes.

The two new endpoints are also the only place this package names a *concrete*
adapter (`OperatorExportAdapter`). That asymmetry is deliberate: the SDK core
stays generic over `SourceAdapter` (ADR-0015), while an HTTP surface has no
choice but to name the thing it exposes, because a caller cannot hand a URL a
Python class.

Status: Demonstrated (drives the real in-memory loop end to end over HTTP);
not Validated, not Production.
info.title: Milexium API

post.description:
Dry-run an operator export sample: which rows would import, which
would quarantine, and why -- WITHOUT storing anything.

NOTHING IS PERSISTED. Concretely, and in the order it matters:

1. The adapter is constructed against `new_id(TenantId)` -- an ephemeral
   tenant that exists for the duration of this call and is registered
   with no store, so the canonical records it produces have nowhere they
   could be written even by mistake.
2. `client.ingest` parses in memory and returns a summary; it issues no
   write (the store is only touched by `record_decision`/
   `record_override`). The parsed records are dropped when this function
   returns.
3. No row VALUE is echoed back. The response carries counts, column
   NAMES, the adapter's own reason text and its semantic-loss reasons.

(3) is what makes this safe to point at a real extract. The adapter
redacts direct identifiers out of its own quarantine record; this
endpoint additionally never returns that record, so a rejected rider
name cannot reach the response even in redacted form -- the operator is
told WHICH COLUMN to strip, which is the actionable part, and is never
shown the value back.

Rows are parsed one at a time through the SDK so each verdict can be
attributed to its row index; the batch runner flattens that.

Localise non-revenue ("empty") vehicle time to hours, days and runs.

The response is the `DeadheadTeardown` itself, NOT an API-local
projection of it. That is the point: the hedging is carried in fields
(`interpretation`, `is_modelled`, `causal_proof`, `manifest.note`,
`manifest.replay_discipline_note`, `cost.hedge`, `cost.envelope_basis`),
and any re-projection here would be a second place those fields could be
dropped from. A caller reading this over HTTP gets the same refusals a
caller holding the Python object does.

What it returns is a MODELLED localisation of where empty time sat --
not causal proof that anything caused it, and not a promised saving. Any
money figure is the accounting value of that time at the operator's own
rate, hedged by the fixed-versus-variable split they supplied (and with
no envelope at all if they did not supply one).

Stateless: no segment, and nothing derived from one, is written to the
canonical store. Verb POST because the body carries the input, not
because anything is created server-side.
